item.title: Aztecs, Cherry throw Thanksgiving block party at Players Era 16 win over Maryland
item.description: SDSU forward Bear Cherry (45) blocks a shot from Maryland guard DJ Wagner (2) during a college basketball game in the Players Era 16 Tournament against Maryland on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. LAS VEGAS — Brian Dutcher talked about the need to protect the rim for San Diego State to have success in an event like the Players Era 16 where size and strength are prevalent just about everywhere. Apparently, Bear Cherry heard his coach. The 6-foot-10 senior center had his own personal block party at Michelob Ultra Arena Thursday, swatting nine Maryland shots, setting a school record for blocks and helping the Aztecs defeat the Terrapins, 75-71. San Diego State (6-1) will play the winner of the Oregon-Texas Tech contest at 8:30 p.m. Friday to wrap up their week in Las Vegas. “No, I actually haven’t,” Cherry said when asked afterward if he had ever blocked so many shots in one game. “I think the most I've ever had is probably like four or five. But it was just my timing. I was just being more patient and waiting, trying to trust my teammates more, and trying to see if they were getting beat or not. I was just catching them at the right time, honestly.” Dutcher said of the accomplishment: “Yeah, nine blocked shots is incredible. Bear is a really good athlete, but I didn't know what kind of shot blocker he would be for us. “He's turned into a great rim protector, and he does it without fouling, which is the key. Bear has got good timing, he's got great athleticism, and a willingness to protect the rim, and that anchors the defense. Whenever you’ve got someone sitting in the back, and you make a mistake, he can contest the shot. It gives you a chance to be a really good defense.” Maryland figured to be a tough out. Buzz Williams has a physical, athletic team and San Diego State had trouble handling Iowa State’s physicality Tuesday in its 81-68 loss to the Cyclones. But they regrouped, reset and handled the Terrapins speed and strength. “This was a good team victory,” Dutcher said. “I like the grit and the toughness of the team. “We enjoyed the first half where everything was going well at the start, and then, like good teams do, Maryland came back and built a six-point lead, but we didn't give in. We hung in there and found a way to be successful. That's what good teams do. We beat them on the glass and got more free throws and those are winning stats.” The Aztecs held a 36-33 edge on the boards and shot 86 percent from the free-throw line (25-29), including Tae Simmons going a perfect 7-for-7 and Latrell Davis going 7 of 8 and Chance Gladden converting on 5 of 6 tries from the stripe. “It all comes down to second chance opportunities, and fast break baskets because it's hard to beat anybody in the half court,” Dutcher said. “We manufactured enough fast break and second chance opportunities to get back in the game and then played Tae Simmons at elbow isolation the last three or four possessions of the game. “I dr

item.title: Sean Miller clowns Matas Vokietaitis after brutal game in win vs. Georgetown
item.description: Dustin Safranek-Imagn Images Sean Miller clowns Matas Vokietaitis after brutal game in win vs. Georgetown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Texas Longhorns defeated the Georgetown Hoyas, 92-83 on Thursday to advance to the championship game of the Rady Children’s Invitational. Through Texas’ first six games of the season, big man Matas Vokietaitis has been a driving force behind the team’s 6-0 start. However, he did not have the best game against Georgetown despite the win, drawing some light humor from Texas head coach Sean Miller, as per Zach Dimmitt of Longhorns on SI. “Matas, he didn’t do anything today,” Miller said. “He had the day off … Matas wasn’t able to play for us today.” Matas Vokietaitis wasn’t exactly invisible for Texas in the win against Georgetown. He had five points and one rebound in 13 minutes of play while shooting 2-of-6 from the field and 1-of-3 from the free-throw line. But those numbers are far below his season averages as he in the midst of a career year. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Vokietaitis has been averaging a career-best 20.7 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.0 blocked shots. He’s shooting 73.4 percent from the field and 66.7 percent from the free-throw line. He had appeared in all six games coming into Thursday’s matchup at just about 26 minutes per game. The junior center is in his second year with the Longhorns after playing his freshman season at Florida Atlantic. With the win, Texas improved to 7-0 on the season. They are currently ranked No. 7 in the AP men’s basketball top-25 poll. This is the program’s second season with Sean Miller at the helm as head coach. Last year, the team finished 21-15, 9-9 in SEC play and were eliminated in the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament by Purdue . item.title: 55 years ago the Dallas Cowboys opened this Super Bowl-winning stadium
item.description: General view of the interior of Texas Stadium during the game between the Washington Redskins and the Dallas Cowboys on September 28, 2008 at Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas. (Tim Umphrey/Getty Images) Dallas Cowboys fans are either celebrating another win or recovering from another loss on Thanksgiving (we don't know at the time of writing). There once was a time when Cowboys fans had almost a guarantee of success on Thanksgiving Day, but those odds seem less and less likely every year. We've already looked at the Cowboys' 30 worst moments in the 30 years since their last Super Bowl , but let's propose that the Cowboys' string of bad luck might be because they demolished their good luck charm. It has now been 55 years since Texas Stadium opened in Irving. The venue debuted in 1971 as the new home of the Dallas Cowboys, who previously played at the Cotton Bowl, and was famous for its hole in the roof that linebacker D.D. Lewis said was "so God can watch His favorite team play." Regardless, the Cowboys had their greatest successes at Texas Stadium, winning all five of the franchise's Super Bowls, including Super Bowl VI the same season Texas Stadium opened. The stadium was demolished in 2010 after the Cowboys moved into AT&T Stadium and the wins have paled in comparison. Coincidence? Let's look at the numbers. Head coach Tom Landry of the Dallas Cowboys stands with his team before coming onto the field before an NFL football game circa 1978 at Texas Stadium in Dallas, Texas. (Focus On Sport/Getty Images) Rear view of Dallas Cowboys QB Troy Aikman (8) in action, passing vs Phoenix Cardinals at Texas Stadium. (Al Tielemans/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) From 1971 through 2008, the Cowboys went 346-240, winning 59% of their games. Since then, it's been a slight drop, going 153-123-1 and winning 55% of games. However, the real impact is seen in the postseason. At Texas Stadium, the Cowboys appeared in 13 NFC Championship Games, played in seven Super Bowls, and won five. Since moving to AT&T Stadium in 2009, the Cowboys have made seven playoff appearances, won four playoff games and have yet to make an appearance in the NFC Championship. So, yes, Cowboys fans can point to many things for their struggles. The departure of Jimmy Johnson, the failures of Barry Switzer, poor choices in the draft, bad free agent signings or countless referee errors. But perhaps it's none of that. Texas Stadium was demolished on April 11, 2010. Perhaps the football gods have not looked kindly on the boys in blue ever since; punishment for choosing the billion-dollar arena over the legacy built in Irving. Ironically, the Cowboys have won four straight games on Thanksgiving heading into this week. So, maybe that's a consolation prize. Victories on Thanksgiving in exchange for heartbreak in winter. item.title: Jeffery Simmons drops mic on Caleb Williams, Bears WRs after clutch heroics vs. Lions
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Jeffery Simmons drops mic on Caleb Williams, Bears WRs after clutch heroics vs. Lions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears moved into sole possession of first place in the NFC North when they delivered a 39-35 victory over the Detroit Lions. The Bears (9-2) used a dramatic fourth-quarter comeback to overcome an 11-point Lions (8-2) lead midway through the fourth quarter. “When you see guys like Caleb and Rome have that connection, it’s not by accident. When you see Caleb and his receivers and tight ends going through their routes when everyone’s off the field, that’s winning football.”🔥 Jeffery Simmons when asked about game-winning touchdown: pic.twitter.com/s3iazKBLCt Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) November 26, 2026 Caleb Williams threw a pair of fourth-quarter TD passes to wide receiver Rome Odunze that allowed the Bears to overcome a huge game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The Detroit star ran for 205 yards and had a 70-yard TD burst in the fourth quarter. That play could have put the game away for the Lions, but Williams was not about to let the Bears accept the defeat and he rallied his team to the dramatic victory. After throwing a 41-yard TD pass to Odunze with 7:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, Williams directed a 13-play, 68-yard drive for the victory. The winning strike was a 6-yard strike to Odunze with 3 seconds left in the fourth quarter. Williams held on to the ball until the last second when he fired a strike to Odunze. The receiver gained possession and got both feet down in the corner of the end zone. Replay confirmed the game-winning play. Star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons was thrilled that his teammates were able to come through with the game on the line. “When you see guys like Caleb and Rome have that connection, it’s not by accident,” Simmons said after the game. “When you see Caleb and his receivers and tight ends going through their routes when everyone’s off the field, that’s winning football.” MORE CHICAGO BEARS NEWS Bears’ Jeffery Simmons calls out Lions for ‘crying’ over Juice Scruggs’ false starts Bears’ TJ Edwards sounds off on clutch 4th-down stop against Jahmyr Gibbs during Lions game Watch Bears HC Ben Johnson’s electric locker room speech after coming back to beat Lions Caleb Williams clears the air on postgame X-Ray, and Bears fans can breathe easy Bears’ Ben Johnson applauds ‘5-star’ TJ Edwards tackle on Jahmyr Gibbs that proved key to Chicago comeback

item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - David Nwaba
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is David Nwaba. An alum of Cal Poly, he went unselected in the 2016 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2017. The Los Angeles, California native played the first season of his pro career with Los Angeles. He also played for the Chicago Bulls and Cleveland Cavaliers before he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2019. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut in 2020. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Nwaba put up 5.2 points and 2.3 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Nets Wire: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - David Nwaba

item.title: What happened the last time Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete at a Grand Slam event
item.description: Jannik Sinner is set to miss the 2026 Australian Open due to injury. The Italian superstar suffered a debilitating knee injury in the lead-up to the US Open and has been absent from the Tour ever since. Sinner underwent knee surgery earlier this week and is now set to spend significantly more time on the sidelines. “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery,” Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo said in a statement to AFP on Thursday. Tennis fans are now set to witness four consecutive Grand Slam events without the presence of both Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner . The last time Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not both compete in a Grand Slam singles event You have to go back seven years to locate the last instance in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete in a single major event. Neither player qualified for the 2019 Wimbledon Championships . Sinner was knocked out in the first round of qualifying by Alex Bolt, and Alcaraz did not make his ATP Tour debut until February 2020 at the Rio Open. At the 2019 Championships, Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer advanced to the men’s singles final in south-west London. Djokovic defeated David Goffin and Roberto Bautista Agut en route to the final, while Federer overcame the likes of Kei Nishikori and Rafael Nadal. What ensued was one of the greatest Grand Slam finals in tennis history. At 7-6, 1-6, 7-6, 4-6, 7-8, Federer led 40-15 and held two championship points on his serve. Djokovic produced some sublime tennis to deny Federer, and eventually won the final set 13-12. Djokovic became the first man since Bob Falkenburg in 1948 to win Wimbledon after being championship points down. “It’s quite unreal,” Djokovic said afterwards. Photo by BEN STANSALL/AFP via Getty Images “Like similar to ’08 maybe, I will look back at it and think, ‘well, it’s not that bad after all’. For now it hurts, and it should, like every loss does here at Wimbledon,” Federer said. “Epic ending, so close, so many moments. Yeah, I mean, sure there’s similarities [between this and his 2008 Wimbledon final loss to Rafael Nadal]. I’m the loser both times, so that’s the only similarity I see.” How did Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner perform in their first Grand Slam events? Alcaraz qualified for his first main draw at a Grand Slam at the 2021 Australian Open. The Spaniard triumphed on his debut, beating Botic van de Zandschulp 6-1, 6-4, 6-4. He was then beaten by Mikael Ymer in four sets. Sinner made his debut 18 months earlier, at the 2019 US Open. The Italian failed to win on debut, losing to Stan Wawrinka in four sets. Sinner secured his first Grand Slam win at the 2020 Australian Open after defeating Max Purcell in straight sets. Marton Fucsovics ended Sinner’s run in the second round, winning 6-4, 6-4, 6-3.

item.title: Meet the ‘Bash Brothers’ of the Utah Mammoth
item.description: Utah Mammoth center Jack McBain (22) and Colorado Avalanche left wing Gabriel Landeskog (92) fight during an NHL game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News Remember the “Bash Brothers” from the second “Mighty Ducks” movie? That’s a thing in the NHL now. OK, nobody in the NHL — or the real world in general — will ever get away with all the blatant interference that Fulton Reed and Dean Portman did in the movie. But Utah Mammoth forwards Jack McBain and Liam O’Brien, who co-lead the league in fighting majors this season, are developing that reputation. View this post on Instagram Anyone who pays close attention to the Mammoth is familiar with the rough-and-tumble personalities of McBain and “Spicy Tuna.” To them, sleeves are optional and facial hair is not. After their interview with the TNT panel after a fiery game against the Colorado Avalanche on Nov. 18, the hockey world got a proper introduction to the swinging fists of the Mammoth. Panelist Paul “Biznasty” Bissonnette, who, according to HockeyFights.com, amassed 200 fights over his 16 years playing junior and pro hockey, even bestowed the “Bash Brothers” nickname upon them. “The NHL is different today than it was even 10 years ago, 20 years ago. I think people sometimes don’t realize that.” Liam O’Brien, Utah Mammoth After some fights tonight, Jack McBain AND Liam O'Brien joined the boys postgame 🥊🔥 Also Biz struck out again asking player to flex... again 😂 pic.twitter.com/Mv1xAzAPCF — NHLonTNT (@NHL_On_TNT) November 19, 2026 Few, if any, NHL tough guys grow up dreaming of filling the role of a fighter. At least in the modern era, they all grew up as skilled players — physicality is just something a player would add to his résumé to both get noticed and provide more value to his team. “As you get older, you’ve got to learn how you can be effective and learn different parts of the game,” McBain said in the TNT interview. “I’m a big guy. I like to play physical, and sometimes that style of hockey makes you have to answer the bell.” O’Brien came just short of a point per game at the U18 AAA level. He flashed a bit of that skill against the Avalanche, scoring on a one-timer and hitting a pair of posts thereafter. He’s known for his physicality, but he came a few inches away from scoring a hat trick in the NHL. When asked whether it feels like people don’t recognize that skill, O’Brien gave an insightful answer. “Yeah, I mean, the NHL is different today than it was even 10 years ago, 20 years ago,” he told the Deseret News. “I think people sometimes don’t realize that. But yeah, that’s fine. “I really don’t care what anybody thinks, to be honest. I know my game. I know my teammates know my game. I know my coaches and my management know my game. So people can say I’m a fighter, enforcer or whatever. It just doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter to me. The only thing that matters is what I am for this team, and that’s just what I focus on.”

item.title: Auburn Football: How to Watch the Tigers Take on Alabama in the Iron Bowl This Weekend
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Auburn Tigers quarterback Byrum Brown (17) passes the ball during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Auburn football is getting ready for one of the biggest games of the 2026 season. The Tigers will travel to Tuscaloosa on Saturday to take on Alabama in the annual Iron Bowl, a rivalry matchup that gives both programs one final opportunity to make a statement before the regular season comes to an end. Head coach Alex Golesh and the Tigers enter the rivalry showdown with a 7-4 record and plenty of momentum. Auburn has won three consecutive games, including a 59-17 victory over Samford last weekend. However, the Tigers will face a much tougher challenge against an Alabama team that enters the matchup at 9-2. The Crimson Tide will have home field advantage at Bryant-Denny Stadium, but Auburn will be looking to pull off a major road victory and finish the regular season with bragging rights. With the Iron Bowl always bringing plenty of intensity, fans should expect an exciting afternoon of SEC football. Here is everything you need to know before kickoff. How to Watch Auburn vs. Alabama Game: Auburn Tigers vs. Alabama Crimson Tide Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Time: 6:30 p.m. CT (7:30 p.m. ET) TV Channel: ABC Streaming: ESPN app Radio: Auburn Sports Network Radio Station: Wings 94.3 FM SiriusXM: Channels 173 and 228 Location: Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama Fubo: DTV: What Will the Weather Be Like? Fans traveling to Tuscaloosa should prepare for a chilly evening at Bryant-Denny Stadium. The current forecast calls for clear skies and temperatures around 52 degrees at kickoff. Rain is not expected to be a concern, with winds around six miles per hour. Temperatures should gradually fall into the upper 40s by the end of the game, so fans attending in person should bring a warm jacket. Overall, the forecast looks favorable for football, with no major weather concerns expected to impact the matchup. Why You Should Watch the Tigers The biggest reason to watch Auburn is the opportunity to see whether the Tigers can finish their regular season with a statement victory. Beating Alabama on the road would be a major accomplishment and give the program plenty of momentum heading into the offseason. Another storyline is the progress Auburn has made under Golesh. The Tigers have won three straight games and will now get an opportunity to measure themselves against one of the SEC’s top programs. The rivalry itself is another reason this game deserves attention. The Iron Bowl is one of college football’s most recognizable matchups, and the intensity between these two programs makes every meeting meaningful. item.title: Cowboys playoff picture: Updated chances for Dallas to make 2026 NFL postseason in Week 12
item.description: Cowboys playoff picture: Updated chances for Dallas to make 2026 NFL postseason in Week 12 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys haven't made the NFC Championship Game in 31 years. In the 2026 NFL regular season, they're just trying to return to the NFC playoffs for the first time in three years. There are low expectations for the Cowboys to make the postseason. They have struggled to get to .500 and stay above it this season. They blew a big chance to even their record by blowing a 31-10 lead in a 39-38 upset loss to the Eagles in Thursday's Week 12 division matchup. With six weeks left, here's breaking down Dallas' updated chances of making the field as NFC East champion or a wild-card team: MORE: Updated NFL playoff picture for Week 12 Cowboys playoff picture The Cowboys (5-7) are down to third place in the NFC East, two-and-a-half games behind the Giants (6-3-1). They are a half-game behind the third-place Commanders (4-5-1). In the big picture of the NFC standings, the Cowboys are No. 11, two-and-a-half games behind the Rams (7-4), who hold the final wild-card position at No. 7. The Seahawks (6-4), Packers (6-5) and Commanders are all between the Rams and Cowboys. Cowboys remaining schedule Week 13: at Seahawks Week 14: bye Week 15: at Rams Week 16: vs. Jaguars Week 17: vs. Giants Week 18: at Commanders The Cowboys, per Tankathon , have a remaining schedule strength of No. 2 in the NFL, as their final five opponents have a combined current winning percentage of .605. The only opponent left with a losing record is Washington. The Seahawks are the most difficult road game. The Jaguars are the most difficult home game. Looking at that gauntlet, finishing 3-2 will keep the Cowboys under .500 at 8-9. The best-case scenario is finishing 9-8 and hoping that's enough to win the division. Dallas' defensive struggles will keep it from going better than 4-1. Cowboys' playoff chances The Cowboys would finish 4-2 in division play if they win the remaining rematches with the Giants and Commanders. Losing the Packers tiebreaker is tough. The Cowboys also cannot afford to lose to both the Rams and Seahawks, and just losing to either can be bad enough. That would make the wild-card path impossible to clear. Then it would be hoping that 9-8 is can still win a weak division. The Giants would then need to finish 2-5 for the Cowboys to win the division. The Cowboys' playoff chances stood at about 15 percent going into Week 12, and they would have improved to only 20 percent with a win over the Eagles. But the shocking loss in their most winnable game puts their chances of making the NFC playoffs at less than 10 percent. MORE: Why Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving

item.title: California’s Top High School Basketball Guards to Watch in 2026-27

The group includes established names from powerhouse programs such as Notre Dame and Sierra Canyon, along with young guards already making a national impression. Here is a look at 13 guards to watch across the 2027, 2028 and 2029 graduating classes. Players are grouped by class and listed alphabetically by last name. Class Of 2027 NaVorro Bowman Jr., Notre Dame, PG — Bowman signed with UConn in September and enters his senior season as one of the nation’s premier point guards. The 6-foot-2 guard is ranked No. 10 nationally in the Rivals Industry rankings and leads a Notre Dame team ranked No. 2 in the Los Angeles Times’ preseason rankings. item.title: Eagles-Cowboys final score: Joe Milton leads comeback victory over Dallas!
item.description: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles throws a pass during second half of an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images HAPPY THANKSGIVING, PHILADELPHIA EAGLES FANS! The Eagles are 4-7 after beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. Final score: 39 to 38. HAHAHAHAHAHAHA. Man, I can’t believe the Eagles won that game! The Birds were looking left for dead after going down 31 to 10 with about three minutes remaining in the third quarter. Their defense was getting carved up by the Cowboys’ high-powered offense. But Joe Milton never said die! The Eagles’ quarterback led his new team to a winning effort against his former team, ultimately finishing 21/31 for 331 yards, three touchdowns, one interception, and a 121.8 passer rating. A lot of that production came through DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards (!) and two touchdowns. Ty Robinson, who blocked a punt to create an Eagles touchdown earlier in the game, came through with a much-needed fourth down sack that ultimately set up a game-winning Jake Elliott field goal! WHAT A WIN! And suddenly the Eagles’ season is not totally dead?! Could they actually win the NFC East?! Probably not … but they weren’t supposed to win this game, either! Next up for the Eagles: a road game against the Arizona Cardinals, which the Eagles will probably be favored in! Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Cowboys took over at their own 23-yard line and Quinyon Mitchell was flagged for pass interference on the first snap from scrimmage. Tacky call on Q going up against George Pickens, who was also pretty handsy on that play. Facing 3rd-and-3, a quick dump off to Javonte Williams resulted in a first down. Cooper DeJean was hurt after tackling Williams. The Cowboys picked up another first down into field goal range with Andrew Mukuba missing a tackle in the hole. Facing 3rd-and-8, Dak Prescott’s first down scramble was called back by Jonathan Greenard drawing a holding penalty on Terence Steele. Facing 3rd-and-18, Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb wiiiiide open in the middle of the field for an easy first down at the seven-yard line. Great resistance there. Not! Jihaad Campbell seemed to get lost in coverage. The Cowboys then went with three straight runs to reach the end zone. 11 plays, 77 yards, 6:10 off the clock. EAGLES 0, COWBOYS 7. The Eagles started at their own 6-yard line after Britain Covey mishandled Brandon Aubrey’s bouncing kickoff. The Eagles picked up their first first down with a Joe Milton completion to Dallas Goedert. Facing 3rd-and-7 after a blitz forced a Milton incompletion, Milton ripped a nice ball to DeVonta Smith for another first down. item.title: Michigan State Gets Past Arkansas, 70-67
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jeremy Fears Jr. #1 and Kur Teng #2 of the Michigan State Spartans celebrate following a made three point basket basket from Teng during the second half against the Arkansas Razorbacks in the CBS Thanksgiving Classic at Little Caesars Arena on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Michigan State Spartans and the Arkansas Razorbacks gave the fans a highly entertaining back-and-forth game on Thanksgiving. I will get to the game in a minute, but first I am going to talk a bit about something that Tom Izzo mentioned at the beginning of his post-game press conference, and that is the Detroit Lions game. Fortunately for me, I live about five minutes from Little Caesars arena so I was able to watch the entirety of the Lions game before darting over for the MSU game. I only missed the first five minutes of the action at LCA. But the end of that Lions game ruined my entire day. And I have to call into question Coach Dan Campbell’s strategy on that last defensive effort. Up three with less than two minutes to go, the best-case scenario is that the Lions would have held the Bears to a field goal. A touchdown, obviously, would be the worst case. With the Bears down to one timeout, they certainly were limited in how many plays they would be able to run. And yet, Coach Campbell helped out the visiting team by using two of his own timeouts. His thought process was that they would be able to hold them to a field goal and then have time left for the offense to do something. But this was not the time to play for the best-case scenario; he should have been more focused on avoiding the worst possible chain of events. Had the Lions not called those two timeouts, Chicago would not have had time for those last two shots at the end zone and they would have had to settle for kicking a field goal right after D’Andre Swift ran it down to the 3-yard line. That is my rant. I think it was a case of poor end-of-game clock management on Campbell’s part. That was a game that the Lions should have at the very least been able to get to overtime. Chicago never should have had that many opportunities to score at the end. Now that I got that out of the way, let’s talk about MSU and Arkansas. By the time I got to my spot along the baseline, the game was about five minutes in. The first half was not the most impressive display of basketball by either team. Both sides struggled to put the ball through the net from all distances. Neither team was able to build much momentum. The largest lead by either side in the first 20 minutes was a 6-point advantage for Arkansas, but that only happened after a long stretch of MSU not scoring rather than Arkansas getting a few in a row. MSU did manage to swing the game back the other way, briefly going up by four with a little over 5 minutes to go. item.title: Code Red for the Orange
item.description: Notre Dame hosts Syracuse on Saturday in the final game of the regular season. Coach Marcus Freeman’s Fighting Irish stand at 10-1 and are seeded fourth in the latest playoff rankings. Meanwhile, the Orange are 5-6, including wins over North Carolina and SMU. Syracuse has improved from a poor 2025 campaign, although their record is disappointing. They will undoubtedly be motivated on Saturday by last year’s 70-7 thumping at the hands of the Irish. The game will be televised nationally by ABC beginning at 12:00 Noon Eastern time. Orange Coach Fran Brown is feeling heat after a disappointing loss to Boston College last week. Starting quarterback Steve Angeli was injured early in the game and did not return. Angeli, who began his career at Notre Dame, will not be able to play on Saturday. He also missed last year’s matchup with the Irish due to an injury. Brown now must defeat Notre Dame to become bowl eligible and win back fan support. On Monday, he discussed the challenge of facing the powerful Irish defense with a liberal dose of coach speak. “I think they’re good on all three levels,” Brown said. “We just want to compete and be able to move the chains. We want to be able to get positive yardage on first, second and third down.” “We’re going to do everything that we can to go out and compete,” Brown added. “We have an opportunity to go up against a good football team. We just need to focus on playing one play at a time against this team, give it all we got and compete every play.” Syracuse does have a bit of history on its side. As a program, the Orange have won four of its last five home games against ranked opponents. This week’s game will be the first sellout of the season in the Carrier Dome. Freeman’s challenge is to ensure the Irish maintain a high standard of play. He was disappointed with his team’s mistakes and penalties last week as well as SMU’s explosive plays. Regarding the Orange, Freeman pointed out the potency of their offense and the challenge it presents. “On offense, they average the most plays in FBS,” he said. “It shows you that they’re sustaining drives and they’re going at a super-fast tempo, which I think you’re seeing a little bit of both as you watch the film. They’re an explosive play offense. They’re gonna take some shots. They’re gonna try to throw the ball over your head and we gotta make sure we do a good job of keeping it in front of us. They do a good job of taking care of the ball. I think they’ve had zero turnovers in four of the last five games.” Notre Dame had been getting healthier until new injuries hit them last week. Jaden Greathouse will miss this game with a wrist injury but is expected back for the playoffs. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa underwent a procedure on his left knee earlier this week. This is the same knee where he has torn his ACL twice. Fortunately, this injury is not as serious. Notre Dame is cautiously optimistic that Viliamu-Asa will be able to return sometime during the playoff calendar. Irish f

item.title: ‘Buffalo will riot’: Fans unhappy with NBC’s Goo Goo Dolls snub during Chiefs-Bills halftime show statement
item.description: Photo by Suhaimi Abdullah/Getty Images One of the biggest talking points ahead of the Buffalo Bills’ game against the Kansas City Chiefs was about the Goo Goo Dolls’ halftime show. It was announced that the American rock band, who are based in Buffalo, New York, would headline the Thanksgiving halftime show at Highmark Stadium. However, less than two hours before the game, NBC announced that they would not broadcast the show. Unsurprisingly, fans are furious. Angry fans react after NBC announces Goo Goo Dolls snubs during Bills vs Chiefs The Goo Goo Dolls are a fan favourite in Buffalo, and many people were really looking forward to their halftime show during the game between the Bills and the Chiefs. However, NBC announced on X and other social channels that they had decided to air Mike Tirico’s discussion with Mike Tomlin about the Pittsburgh Steelers situation instead. NBC released a statement saying: “At halftime of tonight’s Chiefs-Bills game on NBC & Peacock, NBC Sports will air Mike Tirico’s discussion with Mike Tomlin about the Pittsburgh Steelers situation.” It’s safe to say that the fans are not happy. One tweeted: “If they don’t show the Goo Goo Dolls concert, Buffalo will riot.” Another wrote: “Show the Goo Goo Dolls or else the city of Buffalo will be at NBC headquarters by 8 AM tomorrow morning.” “Bills fans don’t freaking care!!! We want the Goo Goo Dolls Halftime show. They are from Buffalo and our favourite. No one cares about Pittsburgh/Tomlin,” said another. Another fan reacted to the statement by saying: “Literally no one watching this game cares about Rodgers. Give us the halftime show!” “This is a terrible move. Families would rather see the halftime show. They can talk Sunday,” posted another. The Goo Goo Dolls’ scheduled halftime show raised the excitement level across Buffalo, and almost every fan had been waiting to watch it on their television sets. However, NBC’s announcement now suggests that the performance will not be aired, which is a huge shame, especially on Thanksgiving. As things stand, the 60,000-odd people who will make it to the Highmark Stadium are the only ones set to catch the halftime show live. item.title: Vital Lazio Midfielder Ruled Out of Torino Trip Amid Injury Fears
item.description: Vital Lazio Midfielder Ruled Out of Torino Trip Amid Injury Fears Lazio have seemingly lost the services of Kenneth Taylor at least for this Saturday’s Serie A contest against Torino. Kenneth Taylor is a Key Player for Lazio The Dutchman has been ever-present in the Biancocelesti’s starting lineup since making the move from Ajax in January this year. The 24-year-old is thus considered a crucial player in Gennaro Gattuso’s tactical scheme and one of the finest midfielders in the Italian top flight. Gattuso Says He Turned Lazio to a Family, Compares Taylor to AC Milan Legend This season, Taylor has contributed with two goals and three assists in 12 league appearances, helping Lazio put together an extraordinary run that placed them at the top of the Serie A table. The Alkamaar native’s exploits in Rome have earned him interest from Juventus, Brentford, Bournemouth, and Newcastle United , but he has already promised Gattuso he will stay at least until the end of the season. Taylor Misses Training With a Muscle Problem Unfortunately for Lazio, Taylor is enduring a physical issue that will rule him out of action for at least one match. According to Il Messaggero , the former Ajax man skipped Wednesday’s training with a muscle issue and only underwent a light pool session on Thursday. Lazio Worried About Taylor for Crucial Matches The player is expected to undergo medical tests on Friday to determine the extent of the problem, but the Roman newspaper is virtually certain he will miss this weekend’s trip to Turin. Torino vs Lazio | Where to Watch, Insights, Lineups & Prediction Therefore, Lazio are anxiously awaiting the results, as Gattuso hopes to have him available for next week’s clash against Atalanta, and more importantly, the Derby della Capitale against Roma (December 13) and the Italian Super Cup versus Inter Milan (December 22). Only Muscle Fatigue? La Lazio Siamo Noi provides a slightly more reassuring initial diagnosis, claiming Taylor is likely suffering from muscle fatigue, but we must await the results of the clinical tests before ruling out any injuries.

item.title: How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident
item.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. All six victims were burnt beyond recognition,” the statement said. Vanguard News The post How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
item.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. She thanked the centre’s partners and funders, assuring that it would continue to provide compassionate care where survivors’ voices mattered. item.title: 18.3m children out of school: Stakeholders demand urgent action
item.description: … NGE challenges govt, media, private sector as UNICEF warns on first 1,000 days By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners yesterday called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million children out of school in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. item.title: Eagles pull off miracle Thanksgiving rally as Cowboys stunningly collapse after disastrous decision
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton (14) runs in for a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with three seconds left to complete the Eagles’ miraculous rally on Thanksgiving. The kick gave Philadelphia a thrilling 39-38 win at AT&T Stadium in a game the Cowboys led 31-10 early in the third quarter. It’s the largest comeback on Thanksgiving in NFL history. Philadelphiaquarterback Joe Miltonruns in for a touchdown during the Eagles 39-38 comeback win over the Cowboys on Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas, who watched kicker Brandon Aubrey miss a 59-yard field goal that would have put them up five on the previous possession, opted to go for it on fourth and 1 from the Eagles’ 39 with 55 seconds remaining, only to see Dak Prescott get sacked. It gave the Eagles the chance to win the game on Elliott’s leg and quarterback Joe Milton’s arm. The Cowboys were still up 14 in the fourth before the Eagles started their improbable comeback by blocking a punt and returning it for a touchdown.

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Bears’ TJ Edwards sounds off on clutch 4th-down stop against Jahmyr Gibbs during Lions game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Jahmyr Gibbs had quite a night on Thursday , but Chicago Bears linebacker TJ Edwards was not going to let the Detroit Lions running back seal the deal in the fourth quarter. With a little over two minutes left in the fourth quarter and the Lions leading by three points, Detroit quarterback Jared Goff threw a short pass to the left to a wide-open Gibbs on a 4th-and-4 at Chicago’s 33. Huge tackle by TJ Edwards to stop Gibbs and the Lions on 4th down! We knew that going in, right?,” Edwards told reporters when asked about his stop on the Lions star tailback, via CHGO Bears. “We knew it was gonna take all eleven getting to the ball, and I saw the look, you know, I knew I knew the coverage. item.title: Friedman: With Ties To Mats Sundin, Simon Edvinsson Could Be Willing To Sign With Maple Leafs
item.description: Follow Michael Whitaker On X We are now just days away from the Dec. 1 deadline by which unsigned RFA Detroit Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson must agree to a new contract or become ineligible to play during the 2026-27 NHL campaign. The Red Wings and Edvinsson have been locked in an awkward standoff dating back to before the current campaign began. The Swedish blueliner reported to training camp in September despite not having a contract and participated in non-scrimmage drills with his teammates. However, frustrated by the lack of progress on a new deal, Edvinsson returned to Sweden before eventually coming back to North America and skating in both Boston and Nashville. His locker in the club's dressing room at Little Caesars Arena has since been occupied by Andreas Englund. What are the chances Edvinsson would sign a contract with Detroit's divisional rival, the Toronto Maple Leafs, if the Red Wings were to trade him there? According to NHL insider Elliotte Friedman, those chances are good. “I’ve heard that Edvinsson is willing to sign there (Toronto)," Friedman said on his latest '32 Thoughts' podcast. "I know there's some people out there who say he'll only sign with Toronto, or that's all he wants to sign with," Friedman continued. "I know that's been all over the interwebs. I don't believe that's true," he said. "I think there are other places he will sign. But I do think he does have interest in Toronto. I just don't know if they can win this." Bookmark The Hockey News Detroit Red Wings team site to stay connected to the latest news , game-day coverage, and player features . Friedman also points to a particular Swedish connection that Edvinsson happens to share with a well-known former Maple Leafs captain and current executive, Mats Sundin. Edvinsson's agent, J.P. Barry, represented Sundin during his Hall of Fame career. "And I think one of the reasons is his agent, J.P. Barry, one of his longest and most beloved clients, was Mats Sundin," Friedman said. "So, you know, like there would be a familiarity there." The Red Wings have already taken care of one major cloud hanging over the organization with Sunday evening's trade of former captain Dylan Larkin. For Edvinsson to play for the Maple Leafs, however, a deal would first need to be worked out with GM John Chayka, who has already shown a willingness to make shrewd transactions. Edvinsson, selected sixth overall by the Red Wings in the 2021 NHL Draft, had developed into Detroit's second-best defenseman behind Moritz Seider. While it's not exactly clear what the holdup is in getting a new contract signed, it remains a mystery how what initially appeared to be a layup of a situation for the Red Wings has now turned into a test of wills with the clock ticking away. item.title: Kenny Smith Faces Backlash After Explaining What Still Makes LeBron James Unstoppable
item.description: IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire ©Credit - Imago LeBron James reminded the basketball world why he remains a postseason nightmare on Wednesday night. By authoring a historic triple-double to lift a shorthanded Philadelphia 76ers squad past the Miami Heat 111–104, he outdid his own record in his 24th season. His performance flipped the Inside Guys’ opinions from skepticism to celebrating his insane productivity. Yet Kenny “The Jet” Smith expressed that praise was a little iffy. With Joel Embiid sidelined by illness and Jaylen Brown exiting before halftime due to left hamstring tightness, LeBron James dusted off the cape, as he claimed. The 41-year-old star delivered 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds, making him the oldest player in NBA history to log a triple-double while pushing the Sixers to an Eastern Conference-best 15–4 record. While Charles Barkley spent the Inside the NBA broadcast questioning whether Philadelphia’s injury-plagued core can survive a seven-game playoff series without adding frontcourt depth, Kenny Smith pushed back on the idea that James is slowing down. Pointing to how James carried the Los Angeles Lakers during the opening round of last season’s playoffs while Luka Doncic was injured, Smith warned the league that James remains dangerous. However, he attributed that longevity largely to modern perimeter rules. “We can’t forget without Luka in the playoffs, he dominated the first round of the series,” Smith said on the broadcast. “And you know, he still has that ability to because, the way the game is played today, obviously, with the lack of handchecking, it is a parallel game. And so what happens is if you’re like a track star, and he can just stay in track shape, and he’s pushing the ball like a track star and not getting touched, not getting slowed down, and he’s still 6’9, 240 lbs, and can still move on a track pace and the NBA is still in danger with him on the floor.” Kenny's take on LeBron's dominance has divided the basketball world. Subscribe to stay on top of the hottest NBA debates and analysis. Chuck had a change of heart, claiming James is “able to score if they need him,” while hyping him as someone who can carry a team. Shaquille O’Neal followed Kenny’s statement with his take on the issue. “At this age, with so many weapons, sometimes he could just sit back and chill. But tonight, the weapons were unavailable , so he did what he had to do. So, you know, he’s smart enough to know when to attack and when to keep everybody involved.” In comparison, Smith’s attempt to compliment James’ conditioning while framing it around the absence of hand-checking did not sit well with fans. What started as a defense of James’ playoff ceiling quickly turned into a heated debate across social media, with fans questioning the logic of suggesting a 250-pound freight train would struggle against physical perimeter contact. item.title: Cricket Australia widens 'Sandpapergate' forum to 2017-2018 Ashes
item.description: Australian fielder Cameron Bancroft (R) is questioned by the umpires after using sandpaper in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 (GIANLUIGI GUERCIA) Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public. The governing body has ruled out reopening its investigation into the explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa that blew up again this month. Instead, it proposed a forum for players, coaches and staff on the tour to share their versions of events. In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0. The hosts' consistent ability to get reverse swing in that series had England's bowlers scratching their heads. In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. "Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing," he said. The issue went no further. Experienced senior counsel Fiona McLeod will lead the forum, which will be open for six weeks and is voluntary. Players' accounts, which can be written or verbal, will be confidential. She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe. McLeod will provide a report detailing the principal themes and her recommendations. But what players say will not be published, no new sanctions will come out of it and she is not charged with determining any individual responsibility. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," said Cricket Australia interim chairman David Boon. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn," added Boon. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." - Reignited - The issue was reignited this month by Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town. He also claimed the practice was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth. A Cricket Australia probe at the time concluded only skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft wer

item.title: 2027: Opposition alliances ‘ll fail again, Fashola declares at APC Lagos rally
item.description: AHEAD of 2027 general elections, former Governor of Lagos State and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has declared that emerging opposition coalitions will suffer the same fate as past failed alliances in Nigeria’s political history. ​Fashola made the assertion yesterday while speaking as the Chief Host at the Babatunde Raji Fashola, BRF Support Group (BRFSG) Campaign kick-off rally, held at the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, where he also launched a grassroots mobilisation drive aimed at building a 10,000-strong volunteer base to secure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the election of Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, as the state’s next governor scheduled for January 16 and February 6, 2027, respectively. The initiative is designed to establish a volunteer-based mobilisation structure across communities, markets, streets and households ahead of the presidential and governorship elections ​ Contrasting the APC 2013 political merger with ongoing talks among rival parties, Fashola, addressing the mammoth crowd of party stalwarts, former heads of service, lawmakers, and students in Lagos, maintained that historical coalitions in 1964, 1983, and 1999 all collapsed without winning the presidency. He dismissed critics who once labeled the APC’s founding blocs as “strange bedfellows,” noting that while the ruling party has consolidated, the opposition has fragmented. ​ “This APC was and remains the only merger that has happened in the history of Nigeria’s political parliament. All of the alliances you have seen on the horizon now will fail too, with your votes,” Fashola told the gathering.Those who see conflict in their party and run away, don’t trust them. They will leave you when things are tough.They don’t stand for anything; they will fall for everything,” he warned. ​​“The intention is to achieve a volunteer party base of 10,000 people, working from now all through to election day, knocking doors, carrying the message of our party, explaining what our party has done, explaining what the candidates have done, explaining what the government has done,” Fashola stated. ​ ​Highlighting the APC’s track record in governance, Fashola pointed to major infrastructure milestones, including: the Lekki Deep Sea Port, the Second Niger Bridge, the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, and the Lagos-Ibadan Railway, as proof of the party’s commitment to long-term economic growth over short-term savings. Hamzat rallies Lagos APC supporters ​The governorship candidate, Hamzat, on his address launched a spirited defence of the ruling party’s governance record, contrasting the APC’s development “blueprint” against what he described as the opposition’s “manifesto of grievances.” ​Addressing the gathering, Hamzat urged APC canvassers to take a bold, fact-based message to voters ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Winners, Losers from Philadelphia Eagles’ Wild 39-38 Win Over Dallas Cowboys
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Thursday night’s Philadelphia Eagles vs Dallas Cowboys matchup on FOX didn’t quite have as much pre-game hype as it usually would given both teams entered Week 12 with a losing record. It proved to be very entertaining, with the Eagles fighting back from a 31-10 deficit in the third quarter with quarterbacks Dak Prescott and Joe Milton putting on a show at AT&T Stadium that came down to a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired. Let’s dive into the winners and losers from the Eagles vs Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day, with Philadelphia delivering a second-half rally for the ages and winning it on a 60-yard field goal. Winner: Javonte Williams, RB, Dallas Cowboys Nov 26, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) runs the ball against Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean (33) during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images It’s worth first revisiting where things stood for Javonte Williams a few years ago. In his final two seasons with the Denver Broncos, he averaged just 3.6 yards per carry with seven touchdowns in 33 games (2023-24). Williams’ career has been revitalized in Dallas. He came into the night with 12 total touchdowns and 914 scrimmage yards in 11 games. He’s now up to a career-high 15 total touchdowns this season, giving him 28 in 28 career games with the Cowboys, after punching in three scores against Philadelphia. Williams also had his third 100-yard game since Week 7. Javonte Williams stats today : 101 rushing yards, 22 receiving yards, 3 total touchdowns Loser: Riq Woolen, CB, Philadelphia Eagles Nov 26, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (3) drops a pass against Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen (2) during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Riq Woolen bet on himself this year, signing a one-year contract with the Eagles hoping a great season would land him a lucrative contract in NFL free agency next season. It’s gone about as poorly as one could imagine. Woolen entered Week 12 having allowed a 105.4 passer rating in coverage this season with nine penalties. The Eagles needed him to step up with Cooper DeJean out, and instead Woolen was torched in coverage and also flagged for defensive pass interference. It probably says something about how he’s viewed around the league that Philadelphia didn’t trade him at the deadline when he clearly doesn’t have a long-term future with the club. Winner: DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) walks off the field after a loss against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Thanksgiving Day provided another reminder of why Eagles general manager Howie Roseman made the A.J. Brown trade. item.title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day

Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. item.title: Joe Milton, Eagles pull off stunning upset vs. Cowboys | How it happened
item.description: Happy Thanksgiving, Philadelphia Eagles fans. Joe Milton and the Eagles pulled off an unbelievable upset win on Thanksgiving, beating the Dallas Cowboys, 39-38, at AT&T STadium. The Eagles trailed by 21 points in the third quarter. It didn’t matter. Nick Sirianni’s team rattled off 22 fourth-quarter points and upended the Cowboys in stunning fashion. Here’s how it happened. FOURTH QUARTER 0:02 — Eagles 39, Cowboys 38 Unbelievable. Jake Elliott drilled a 60-yard field goal to win it. JAKE ELLIOTT FROM 60 YARDS OUT EAGLES COMEBACK IS COMPLETE PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LJoGRn56xr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 2:10 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 36 Joe Milton did it again. Unbelievable. The cannon-armed QB engineered a four-play, 70-yard touchdown drive, ending in a 24-yard strike to Makai Lemon in the back of the end zone. The Eagles’ defense has to come up with a stop to get the ball back for Milton and the offense to pull off the upset. 9:09 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 30 And just like that, the Eagles are back in it. Joe Milton is having a day. After a 55-yard kickoff return by Britain Covey, the Eagles needed only three plays to find the end zone. Two completions to DeVonta Smith preceded Milton’s 15-yard touchdown scramble to cut the Cowboys’ lead. Nick Sirianni decided to go for the two-point conversion, and the Eagles didn’t get it. But this is yet again a game. JM3 TAKING OFF pic.twitter.com/uOmx34nE6S — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 27, 2026 10:11 — Cowboys 38, Eagles 24 Just like that, the Cowboys answer. Quinyon Mitchell got put on skates by Ceedee Lamb, who ripped off a 39-yard catch-and-run into Eagles’ territory. A few plays later, Dak Prescott went airborne for an acrobatic, 14-yard touchdown scramble to make it a two-score game again. INSANE EFFORT BY @dak 🤯 📺: #PHIvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/J9HR0OTmZi — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 27, 2026 13:46 — Cowboys 31, Eagles 24 Well, well, well. We have a game. After a huge defensive stop on third-and-short, defensive tackle Ty Robinson blocked the Cowboys’ punt, and Kenny Moore returned it for a touchdown. Just like that, the Eagles are back in it. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 THIRD QUARTER 0:15 — Cowboys 31, Eagles 17 This Joe Milton-DeVonta Smith connection has been fun to watch. For the second time, Milton uncorked a bomb downfield for Smith. The Eagles’ WR1 was wide op

item.title: Stay away from our state, Imo APC tells Wike
item.description: The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Imo State, has declared that the state is not available for political manipulation or interference by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike. Read Also: ‘I’m done with Rivers, FCT; give me Imo, Kwara to deliver’ – Wike tells Tinubu It vowed to resist any attempt to import what it described as his controversial political tactics into the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party made its position known in a statement yesterday by its State Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones in reaction to alleged Wike’s recent claim that he had concluded arrangements to secure electoral victories for President Bola Tinubu and the APC in the forthcoming elections. Wike was also reported to have offered to undertake additional political assignments for the President, including delivering other states for the APC. Reacting, the Imo APC dismissed the minister’s claims, contending that he should not assume that his political activities could determine the electoral fortunes of the party in different states. The statement particularly faulted Wike for reportedly suggesting that Imo State and another APC-controlled state had political problems requiring his intervention. “We would have ignored the politically displaced errand boy, like we always do, but for the fact that we deem this particular statement of his a direct affront on the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the electoral integrity of our dear party, the APC,” the statement declared. The party accused the FCT minister of attempting to portray President Tinubu as politically dependent on individuals outside the APC to secure electoral victories, insisting that the party enjoys its own grassroots support and political structure. It also faulted Wike’s reported assertion that he had already secured victory for the APC in the FCT and Rivers State, describing such declarations, made weeks before the elections, as disrespectful to democratic principles and the electorate. According to the statement, “our party, the All Progressives Congress, has immense regard for the Nigerian people and would not encourage actions and utterances that tend to cast the Nigerian electorate as irrelevant in the determination of their political future.” The Imo APC further accused Wike of taking advantage of the party’s political goodwill to sustain his relevance while allegedly making disparaging remarks about some of its leaders. It challenged the minister to demonstrate his political influence by campaigning for his own party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), rather than making claims about delivering APC victories. On the political situation in Imo State, the party maintained that its activities were progressing without difficulty and expressed confidence in its preparations for the 2027 elections. It said its mobilisation efforts across the state were ongoing, adding that it expected Imo voters to participate in the forthcoming elections

item.title: Security chiefs hail IGP Disu for suspending declaration of Obaigbena, others wanted
item.description: By Emma Nnadozie THE police order suspending the wanted declaration on Arise TV owner, Mr. Nduka Obaigbena and seven others over alleged assassination attempt by Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Olohundare Jimoh, has elicited reactions from some security chiefs in the country, who said that the wanted declaration was done without due process. One of the security chiefs who spoke with Vanguard, said: “It was misappropriate and procedurally flawed” and showered encomiums on the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his quick response by suspending the wanted declaration The Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Zone 2, Onikan, Lagos, Olohundare Jimoh, last Tuesday, declared Chairman of Arise News and This Day Media Group, Chief Nduka Obaigbena, Managing Director of Nestoil, Dr. Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi, and seven others wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu in a crowed press conference in Lagos. He said the declaration followed an investigation into the delivery of a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition to Alebiosu’s residence in Lagos. However, in a swift reaction two days later, the IGP, through the Force Public Relations Officer, FPRO, Ani Iniedu suspended the wanted declaration against the suspects and stated that the case has been transferred to the Force Intelligence Department, FID, Abuja, for a thorough and impartial investigation. He also directed the nine individuals to report to the FID, at the Force headquarters , Abuja, between November 26 and 30, 2026. In his reaction, the Director-General of the Institute of Security, Nigeria at the University of Lagos, Mr. Adebayo Akinade, said that the Zone 2 declaration was “misappropriate and procedurally flawed. The IGP’s suspension and transfer to Force Intelligence Department was correct, strategic and has restored public confidence.” Former Director with the Department of State Service, DSS, and currently a security consultant, Mr. Mike Ejiofor, said: “The IGP has the superior order on such matters. When a subordinate makes a mistake, the IGP is in a position to correct it. So, I do not see any conflict in the matter.” In his response the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of Perfect Security Services Limited, Dr. Patrick Uwagbale saw the incident as “part of a system that is not in order. A good society will do something according to the rules. Even if the allegation is true or not, it is unheard of that someone as IGP would be on seat and a subordinate had the audacity to take such a decision on such a high profile incident without authorisation from the IGP who ordinarily should have the last say on such a matter. This type of behaviour clearly shows that our system is not healthy. “Something is wrong somewhere. There is a gap somewhere. I wholly support the decision of the IGP to suspend the declaration by his subordinate.” Recall also that The Chairman of This Day Newspapers and Arise, Nduka Obaigbena

item.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. Violence may suppress voter turnout The INEC chairman identified three major consequences of political violence for the electoral process, including voter suppression, threats to the safety of electoral personnel and the possibility of post-election violence.
