item.title: The token factory never sleeps
item.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30

item.title: PDP will reclaim Ebonyi in 2027, chairman declares
item.description: …As Odii receives flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwu Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates in the state. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP stronghold since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The national chairman further alleged that the PDP won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that the party would reclaim its mandate in 2027. He urged residents to vote for PDP candidates, saying the party was determined to change the state’s economic fortunes. In his acceptance speech after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The PDP candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said that despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, he said, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. He further alleged that the government spent less than its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget. The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state. He said his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families. According to him, the foundation also supports over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and has empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, in addition to executing rural electrification and road projects. Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings. He said his administration would pursue an integrated infrastructure programme covering roads

item.title: Kitto violence: Majority of victims suffer in silence – ISHRAI warns
item.description: .. Only 28% of victims report attacks, survey across six South-West states reveals By Chioma Obinna A growing pattern of online deception, blackmail, sexual exploitation and extortion is exposing young Nigerians and other vulnerable people to physical attacks, psychological trauma and even death, with a survey revealing that 71.3 per cent of respondents across six South-West states had experienced Kitto-related violence. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. The Improved Sexual Health and Rights Advocacy Initiative (ISHRAI), which disclosed the findings, raised the alarm over the trend, warning that victims were increasingly exposed to kidnapping, sexual abuse, blackmail, mob attacks and other forms of violence. The organisation called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, women and youth groups to intensify community awareness, protect vulnerable people and discourage public shaming, discrimination and jungle justice. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement involving traditional and religious leaders, ISHRAI’s Programme Manager, Mrs Sophia Lawal, said community leaders must be equipped with the knowledge and referral mechanisms to identify cases of Kitto-related violence and respond appropriately. Lawal said the engagement brought together 20 traditional and religious leaders, including women leaders, to deliberate on the threats facing marginalised people and develop community-based responses. “It’s very important that we have community members, that’s the religious, traditional leaders, and also the women leaders, to have conversations around kitto violence that affects marginalized people in Nigeria,” she said. “And we cannot address these issues without having the right people in the room to deliberate on this matter together so that they are equipped with the right, with the knowledge to actually handle such cases when they are being reported or how to even identify such cases in their immediate community.” Providing details of the survey, an ISHRAI representative said 240 people were interviewed across the six South-West states, with 71.3 per cent indicating that they had experienced Kitto-related violence. He said the organisation’s intervention was aimed at reducing the practice through public education, early identification and effective community response. Explaining how perpetrators operate, he said many exploit social media to establish relationships with unsuspecting young men and women, build their confidence and lure them into physical meetings under false pretences. item.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
item.description: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

item.title: ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt
item.description: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours of a postponement of the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, confirming that it will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The exercise is scheduled to take place between 6:30am and 8:30am and will be monitored by government officials across various local government areas and local council development areas. The state government made the clarification on Thursday in a statement signed by Kunle Adeshina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The statement quoted the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, as saying there was no basis for postponing the exercise. “There is no basis to cancel the monthly exercise which has become a rallying point for everyone to stay back and clean their neighbourhood,” Tajudeen said. He added that the November edition would be monitored across the state, as had become a tradition. According to the statement, the First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, will lead a team of government officials to monitor the exercise in Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Similarly, another team led by the Head of Service, Mr Olabode Agoro, will monitor activities in Coker-Aguda Local Council Development Area. Explaining the timing of the exercise, Tajudeen said the 6:30am to 8:30am schedule would allow residents to participate in the clean-up without disrupting other activities. He said the timeframe “gives enough room for any form of civic exercise to still be undertaken after the clean-up.” The permanent secretary urged Lagos residents to remain in their neighbourhoods and participate actively in the exercise. He also called on transport unions to use the opportunity to clean their parks and garages before resuming passenger operations at 8:30am. The state government reiterated its call for collective participation in maintaining environmental cleanliness across Lagos State. item.title: Ramaphosa hosts Obasanjo, AFC delegation for Africa infrastructure talks
item.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has met with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and a delegation from the African Finance Corporation (AFC) to discuss infrastructure development and investment opportunities across the continent. The meeting, held at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, was led by AFC President and Chief Executive Officer, Samaila Zubairu. Discussions focused on the forthcoming Africa We Build Summit, scheduled to take place in Johannesburg from April 28 to 30, 2027. A statement from the presidency reads in part, “The summit is expected to highlight infrastructure development at a time when African countries are pursuing an ambitious pipeline of cross-border projects aimed at strengthening regional connectivity and economic integration. “Through the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), 69 priority projects are currently at various stages of implementation across the continent. However, advancing the projects requires sustainable and predictable financing, alongside stronger partnerships between governments, development finance institutions and private investors.” The discussions between Ramaphosa, Obasanjo and the AFC delegation underscored the importance of mobilising investment and strengthening cooperation to translate Africa’s infrastructure ambitions into tangible development outcomes. The Africa We Build Summit is expected to provide a platform for stakeholders to explore financing opportunities, strengthen partnerships and accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure projects across the continent. 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party. The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties. She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state. Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence. She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement. The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace. She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements. In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections. They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities. The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections. item.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. item.title: PDP vows to reclaim Ebonyi in 2027
item.description: ..Odii receives party flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwuma Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the party’s campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP-controlled state since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The PDP chairman further claimed that the party won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that it would recover its mandate in 2027. He appealed to residents to vote massively for the PDP to change the state’s economic fortunes. Speaking after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected. The governorship candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents. He said despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, according to him, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He also questioned the state government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined. He further alleged that the government spent below its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget. The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state. He disclosed that his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families. According to him, the foundation has also supported over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, alongside rural electrification and road projects. Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings. The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United. Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires. Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid. If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side. Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand. item.title: 2027: Ogun ADC accepts Supreme Court ruling, backs Ogundipe as guber candidate
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accepted the Supreme Court ruling affirming Biodun Collins Ogundipe, popularly known as BCO, as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on aggrieved members to close ranks and work together for the success of the party at the polls. The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Executive Committee, local government area (LGA) chairmen, party leaders, elders and other stakeholders held on Thursday. The meeting, presided over by the State Chairman, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, considered the Supreme Court judgment alongside a letter dated November 23, 2026, from the party’s National Legal Adviser, which, according to the state chapter, reinforced the need for the party to operate within the provisions of the law. In a communiqué issued at the end of the meeting, the Ogun ADC said it had resolved to accept the apex court’s decision without prejudice and recognise Ogundipe as the party’s duly affirmed governorship candidate in the state. The party described its position as a demonstration of respect for the rule of law and the need to preserve the party’s unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. The development is expected to provide a fresh direction for the party’s preparations in Ogun State, particularly against the backdrop of leadership and governorship candidacy disputes that had generated disagreements among members. The communiqué further disclosed that Otunba Jimi Adebisi Lawal (JAL) and members of his campaign council had pledged their commitment to supporting the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, as well as all the party’s candidates in Ogun State. According to the communiqué, the party leadership has resolved to mobilise its entire political structure across the state to ensure victory for its candidates in the forthcoming elections. It said the mobilisation drive would extend across all levels of the party, including the state, local government, ward and polling unit structures. The party also reaffirmed its commitment to working collectively for the success of its candidates contesting the presidential, governorship, senatorial, Federal House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections. It added that political activities would be intensified in the months ahead to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, expand its support base and consolidate its electoral prospects ahead of 2027. Speaking on the need for reconciliation, Soluade appealed to party members, leaders and stakeholders to put aside their differences and unite behind the party’s collective ambition. He urged party loyalists and political stakeholders to shun bickering, divisive tendencies and unnecessary internal disagreements, emphasising that unity and cooperation were essential to the ADC’s success. item.title: AC Milan rally from two goals down to beat Olympiakos
item.description: Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos. Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knock-out phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Joao Silva’s 49th-minute strike. But Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the former Ipswich winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute. Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth, breathing life into the seven-time European champions’ campaign. Belgians Union Saint-Gilloise are fifth in the standings, one point behind Leverkusen, Ferencvaros and Benfica, after preserving their unbeaten record, also coming back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Lech Poznan. – Clashes in Georgia – The Turkish Football Federation condemned “unacceptable” scenes as Georgian police clashed with Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner. The Istanbul team’s game against Hapoel was being played in Batumi due to security reasons. “We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the UEFA Europa League match between our representative Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia,” the club said. A Turkish ministry source said Turkey’s top diplomat, Hakan Fidan, had spoken with his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili. “Officials from the Turkish Embassy in Tbilisi and the Consulate General in Batumi are at the stadium,” the source said. “All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights.” There were also violent clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters during the Ligue 1 club’s 1-0 win in France. Brighton moved second in the Conference League table by swatting aside Universitatea Craiova of Romania 4-0. Ghana international Ibrahim Osman scored his first goals for the high-flying Premier League club with a double, with Maxim De Cuyper and Charalampos Kostoulas also on the scoresheet. Fabian Hurzeler’s side are two points behind leaders Monaco, who edged out Hearts 3-2 at Tynecastle courtesy of Folarin Balogun’s 94th-minute winner. item.title: Gbajabiamila leads Tinubu’s delegation to IBB, Abdulsalami
item.description: Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Femi Gbajabiamila, on Thursday led a presidential delegation to Minna, Niger State, to pay courtesy visits to former military Heads of State, Generals Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar. Gbajabiamila disclosed this in a statement, saying the visit was undertaken at the directive of President Tinubu to convey his goodwill and best wishes to the two elder statesmen. He said the delegation was warmly received by both former leaders, who appeared well and in high spirits during the visits. According to him, Babangida expressed satisfaction with the Tinubu administration’s performance, reaffirmed his support for the President and wished him success. Abdulsalami, on his part, commended the administration’s performance and thanked Tinubu for remembering the former leaders despite the demands of the ongoing election campaign. Gbajabiamila described the two former leaders as important figures in Nigeria’s history, noting that their experience and counsel remained invaluable to the country. “These are men who occupy major chapters in Nigeria’s history and their counsel remains invaluable,” he said. He added that the President was pleased with their support and expressed optimism about their continued backing in the coming elections. The visits come amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties and their candidates intensify consultations and mobilise support across the country. Babangida, who ruled Nigeria from 1985 to 1993, remains one of the country’s most influential former military leaders, while Abdulsalami, who assumed power in June 1998, oversaw the transition programme that ushered in the Fourth Republic in May 1999.

item.title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
item.description: We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home • The best office chairs Fast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office. Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home. item.title: 32 Years Later, Disney's Most Notorious Cash-Grab Sequel Is Better Than You Remember
item.description: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and res

item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

item.title: Indie web browser Ladybird enters alpha testing
item.description: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't

item.title: NAF: Tinubu Approves ₦100m, Houses For Families Of Air Crash Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. We could not bring them home to you, and our inability to recover their remains has made this harder still. But hear me, the sky did not take their honour. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. item.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
item.description: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

item.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
item.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
item.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
item.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: The best Black Friday deals we’ve already found
item.description: The countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. item.title: ORLSON seeks improved hearing care, specialist training as ENT experts meet in Kano
item.description: The Otorhinolaryngological Society of Nigeria (ORLSON) has called for urgent government intervention to address critical gaps in ear and hearing healthcare services across the country, citing inadequate infrastructure, shortage of specialists, rising cost of treatment and limited access to modern medical technologies. The call formed part of resolutions reached at the end of the Society’s 34th Annual General Meeting and Scientific Conference held from November 18 to 21 at the Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria (MAAUN), Kano. The resolutions are contained in a communique issued at the end of the conference and signed by ORLSON outgoing President, Professor Aliyu Mohammed Kodiya, and the outgoing Secretary, Dr Enema J. Amodu. The conference, which was held under the theme, “Advancing Otological Services in Nigeria: Bridging Gaps in Infrastructure, Training and Service Delivery,” brought together ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialists, resident doctors, audiologists, nurses, speech and language professionals, researchers, academics, healthcare administrators, development partners and industry stakeholders from within and outside Nigeria. A communiqué issued at the end of the four-day gathering highlighted growing concerns about the burden of preventable ear diseases and hearing loss in Nigeria and emphasized the need for a coordinated national response to improve access to quality ear and hearing care services. Wide-ranging deliberations The conference featured scientific presentations, panel discussions, workshops and stakeholder engagements that focused on various aspects of otorhinolaryngology, including otology, audiology, paediatric ENT practice, rhinology, laryngology and head and neck surgery. Participants examined challenges confronting hearing healthcare services in Nigeria and reviewed recent developments in clinical practice, training and research. As part of activities marking the conference, delegates paid courtesy visits to the management of the Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria, Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital and the Emir of Kano. The event was officially declared open by a representative of the Kano State Government, while participants also reviewed the progress of the professional body and conducted elections that produced a new National Officers Committee. ORLSON further used the occasion to showcase activities of its Abuja Secretariat and highlight ongoing efforts aimed at strengthening its digital platforms and institutional structures. Infrastructure deficit remains major challenge The society ORLSON seeks improved hearing care, specialist training as ENT experts meet in Kano that despite increasing demand for hearing and ENT services, many healthcare facilities across the country still lack adequate infrastructure and equipment needed for effective diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of patients. item.title: Detty December Finds Its Crown: Green Indie Artistry 2026
item.description: There is a burst of energy and undeniable excitement that comes over a room when the crowd realises it has power. It happened at BallR Lagos in December 2024, when Green Indie and Hennessy staged the first Indie Star Search finale. The lights dropped, the names were read, and the verdict was something the audience helped write. On Thursday, 17 December 2026, that idea returns bigger. Green Indie Artistry opens at 5:00 PM at Baywater Park, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos. The headliners are 9ice, Fido, and JAYBERRY . Four DJs keep the floor moving between sets. And at the center of the night sits the Indie Star Search, where four finalists perform for the people who will decide who wins. It is less a concert than a referendum with a dance floor. The Premise: Judged by the Room Most competitions are decided behind closed doors. Green Indie flips that. Four finalists perform live, and everyone holding a pass votes on the sets. That audience vote carries its weight in the result. The format has a sharp edge. The people who paid to be in the room become accountable for what happens in it. If the winner is an artist you championed from the front, you helped put them there. The competition has history. The inaugural Indie Star, Young Incredible, won in 2024 with “Lagos to Abuja” and walked off under a storm of confetti. The four finalists for 2026 will be revealed on 6 December. The Headliners The live bill is built on contrast, and that is deliberate. 9ice legendary entertainer, bringing decades of Lagos street credibility into a room full of emerging talent. This is a statement about continuity: the old guard is standing next to the new one. Fido is a performance you don’t want to miss, because you know Joy is coming! For a night that asks the crowd to care who wins, a distinctly local identity is a useful anchor. JAYBERRY brings vibrant energy with heartfelt lyrics. That pairing is harder than it sounds. Energy without substance is cho cho cho; substance without energy is a let down. Access is tiered, and the structure is worth understanding before you buy. All tickets available here . VS: General admission: ₦20,000 (about $16 on an international card). VSOP table, seats 4 XO table, seats 7 The tiers are named for the drinks poured on the night, which suits a Hennessy-backed event. The tables are clearly built for groups who want a base for the night, not just a spot at the rail. Why It Matters Beyond One Night Green Indie describes itself as Africa’s first Direct-to-Fan music platform, selling music directly to listeners rather than routing it through labels. Indie Star Search is the most visible expression of that philosophy: it hands part of the discovery decision to the audience. Whether or not you buy the platform’s broader claims, the event tests an idea. In a creative economy where algorithms often decide what gets heard, a room that votes in real time offers a different signal. It is messier, louder, and more human. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
item.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. "We need to understand what is working, where things are falling short and, crucially, what needs to change," said DCMS Secretary Lisa Nandy. The watchdog won't have to wait long for its

item.title: Rocket Lab sending Japanese satellite to orbit on Thanksgiving Day launch: Watch it live
item.description: null Rocket Lab will add another satellite to a growing Japanese Earth-observation constellation today (Nov. 26), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket carrying a radar imaging satellite for Tokyo-based Earth-observation company Synspective is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab 's New Zealand launch site today, during a window that opens at 7:00 p.m. ET (0000 GMT and 1:00 p.m. on Nov. 27 in New Zealand). You can watch the mission, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before liftoff. Space.com will carry the company's stream if, as expected, it's made available. Synspective is building a network of "Strix" spacecraft equipped with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which uses radio waves to generate detailed images of Earth's surface in both day and night lighting, as well as through cloud cover. Today's launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th for Synspective to date, and there are a lot more coming. At the end of September, Rocket Lab announced a deal with the company for an additional 20 Electron missions between 2028 and 2031 — the largest commercial launch contract in the rocket's history. That agreement brought Synspective's total number of contracted Electron flights to 47. Synspective aims to eventually establish a constellation capable of imaging locations anywhere on Earth at intervals of just a few hours. The patch for Rocket Lab's "Night Owls Never Sleep" mission. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) If all goes to plan today, the Electron's kick stage will deploy the Strix satellite into low Earth orbit , 569 kilometers (353.6 miles) above our planet. "Night Owl Never Sleeps" will be the 101st mission to date for Rocket Lab. Ninety-two of them have been orbital flights with Electron; the other nine have been missions with HASTE , a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test sensors and other equipment in the hypersonic flight environment.

item.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace , picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. One case that resembles the early days of bitcoin was the war of the currents between high-voltage AC current and low-voltage DC current in the 1880s-1890s. Both featured big personaliti
